subunit: Heterodimer of an alpha chain and a beta chain. Beta-2-microglobulin is the beta-chain of major histocompatibility complex class I molecules. Polymers of beta 2-microglobulin can be found in tissues from patients on long-term hemodialysis. B2M alone (not in complex with HLA-I) interacts with M.tuberculosis EsxA (ESAT-6) and an EsxA-EsxB (CFP-10) complex; the tripartite complex can be detected in the host endoplasmic reticulum. The B2M-EsxA complex can be detected in patients with pleural tuberculosis and is stable from pH 4.0 to 8.0 and in the presence of 2M NaCl. Forms a heterotrimer with HLA-E and a self- or a foreign peptide. Forms a heterotrimer with HLA-G and a self-peptide. Forms a heterotrimer with HLA-F and a self-peptide. Forms a heterotrimer with MR1 and a metabolite antigen

complexes.name: Classical MHC Ia complex, HLA-A-B2M
complexes.function: Antigen-presenting major histocompatibility complex which presents the bound peptide antigen to CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes. The complex assembles in the endoplasmic reticulum and is transported to the cell surface. Presents primarily viral and tumor-derived peptides
complexes.properties: Two membrane-distal domains (alpha-1 and alpha-2) form a groove that binds to a peptide of 8-11 amino acids. B2M stabilizes the conformational orientation of the peptide binding groove associating with a third domain (alpha-3) and restricts the peptide length in the groove. Polymorphism of the MHC proteins results in different peptide-binding grooves that recognize unique peptides owing to variations in the anchor residues to which peptides dock.

complexes.name: CD1B-B2M complex
complexes.function: An antigen-presenting complex that binds self and non-self lipid and glycolipid antigens and presents them to T-cell receptors on natural killer T-cells. The antigen binding specificity of CD1B is very broad in terms of length of the acyl chains. CD1B also presents endogenous gangliosides, such as GM1, to specific T cells, suggesting their involvement in autoimmune diseases such as multiple sclerosis.
complexes.properties: The antigen-binding groove houses four interlinked hydrophobic channels denoted as A prime, C prime, F prime and T prime. Total volume of the binding groove is 2200 A^3 and can accomodate hydrophobic chains of up to 80 carbons.
